sections.h2: How does selling a house in Newnan, GA work?
sections.html:
Newnan sellers choose between three routes: list with an agent, sell directly to a buyer, or accept an as-is cash offer, and the right one depends on how much work the house needs and how soon you must close. Newnan is the Coweta County seat, about 35 miles southwest of Atlanta along Interstate 85, and covers roughly 19.5 square miles.

The Census Bureau estimates 45,867 residents on July 1, 2025, up 8.0% from the 42,451 counted at the April 2020 base. Its 2020 to 2024 survey figures show 17,180 households, a 58.2% owner-occupied rate, a median owner-occupied home value of $364,700 and median gross rent of $1,542. Those are citywide averages. A cottage near the square and a newer subdivision house on the edge of town can sit far apart from them, so ask for recent sold homes in your own neighborhood.

sections.h2: What is special about Newnan's housing stock?
sections.html:
The city was incorporated in 1828 and laid out on a grid with a nine-block downtown centered on the courthouse. Its streets carry names such as Jackson, Jefferson, Washington and Madison. Railroad money and cotton wealth in the mid 1800s left a large stock of antebellum and Victorian houses, and the city still calls itself the "City of Homes."

Newnan's historic district page names seven districts. Several are residential, and each has its own character:

  • Cole Town grew around the R.D. Cole woodworking company, and its trim details define the houses.
  • College-Temple, laid out in 1828, has tree-lined streets, churches and a long run of architectural styles.
  • Greenville-LaGrange is a 61-acre area along two major highways with the oldest and largest houses on the principal streets.
  • Platinum Point is a 43-acre collection of early 20th century homes built north of town.
  • Newnan Cotton Mill and Mill Village includes a mill that is now a loft apartment complex.
  • Chalk Level, in southeast Newnan, was added to the Georgia Register of Historic Places on October 24, 2025 and to the National Register on January 29, 2026.

If your house sits in one of these districts and you or a buyer plan exterior changes, call Newnan Planning and Zoning at 770-254-2354 to ask whether design review applies before work starts.

sections.h2: What permits and city rules affect a Newnan seller?
sections.html:
The Building Department is on the second floor of City Hall at 25 LaGrange Street, open Monday through Friday from 8 a.m. to 4:30 p.m. A permit application needs, at minimum, a site plan, a building plan, a ResChek or Comchek compliance report, contractor licenses, a subcontractor list and the fees. If you did past work yourself, pull whatever record exists, because an unrecorded addition tends to surface during a buyer's inspection.

Tree work is the other local rule sellers run into. Per the city's FAQ, a homeowner pays nothing to remove trees on their own single-family lot until more than five come down at one time in a calendar year, while a paid contractor needs a tree removal permit for any tree eight inches or more across. Specimen trees are treated separately, so ask before cutting one.

Getting to a showing is straightforward. The city's directions send northbound drivers to I-85 Exit 47, then three miles west on Highway 34, and southbound drivers to Exit 41, then 3.5 miles north on Highway 29. Newnan's combined sales tax is 7 percent, made up of 4 percent state tax and 1 percent each for LOST, ESPLOST and SPLOST.

sections.h2: Which Coweta homestead exemptions can a Newnan buyer or seller claim?
sections.html:
Coweta County grants a basic homestead exemption to people who own and occupy their home on January 1, and its senior school tax exemptions carry no income limit. The county's exemption page lists these local school tax tiers for 2026:

Coweta senior school tax exemptions, 2026
CodeAge as of January 1Exemption from school taxes
LC65$75,000
LE71$100,000
LG75Full exemption

Source: Coweta County Exemptions page. The county notes these can stack with the disabled veteran exemption on a separate application, and that locally enacted exemptions override the state amount when they are larger.

A seller who qualified should remind the buyer that the exemption does not follow the house. The new owner files fresh with the Assessors' Office, and the county says an individual or married couple can claim only one homestead exemption.

sections.h2: How do Coweta property taxes and appeals work for a Newnan house?
sections.html:
The Coweta Assessors' Office at 37 Perry Street sets values, and the Tax Commissioner at 87 Newnan Station Drive bills and collects. The 2026 assessment notices were mailed on June 19, and the 45-day window to appeal closed on August 3, 2026. Each year's notice prints its own deadline, so read the date on yours.

Bills go out in October. The Tax Commissioner mails each one to the legal owner of record as of January 1 and also to the most recent owner shown in the Assessors' records, so both sides of a late-year sale see a bill. If an appeal is unsettled when bills are printed, the owner gets a temporary bill based on 85% of the Assessors' proposed value, and settlement leads to either a partial refund or extra tax due. The 2026 bills also show the state's Homeowner Tax Relief Grant credit on residential homestead property.

Escrow customers should send a copy of the bill to their lender, since the county warns that mortgage companies often pay only a few weeks before the due date. Card payments carry a processing fee of 2.5% (3% for American Express), and online e-checks carry a $1.50 fee. For a specific parcel, call the Assessors at 770-254-2680 or the Tax Commissioner at 770-254-2670.

sections.h2: Where are Newnan deeds recorded, and what does recording cost?
sections.html:
Every Coweta real estate record is kept by the Superior Court Clerk's Real Estate Division, and documents are recorded daily in the order they arrive. The clerk lists a $25 filing fee for deeds, $10 for plats, $1 per page for copies and $2.50 for the first page of a certified copy. Personal checks are not accepted, and card payments add a surcharge.

The PT-61 transfer tax declaration must be e-filed with every title change. Under the clerk's rules, self-filers must e-file after identity verification, while Georgia-licensed attorneys, lenders, title companies, surveyors and licensed brokers may file on paper. In practice your closing attorney handles this. The Georgia Department of Revenue sets the transfer tax at $1 for the first $1,000 of price plus 10 cents per additional $100 or fraction, owed by the seller unless the contract shifts it to the buyer, and the clerk certifies payment on the deed.

Coweta also offers free real estate fraud alerts through the Georgia Superior Court Clerks' Cooperative Authority. A seller who still owns other parcels in the county, or an heir holding an inherited deed, can sign up for notices.

sections.h2: Should I list, sell myself, or take a cash offer in Newnan?
sections.html:
A traditional listing suits a house in decent shape and a seller who can wait through showings, appraisal and lender timelines. Selling without an agent saves the commission and puts pricing and paperwork on you. A cash buyer purchases the house as-is, often closing in a few weeks, and the price reflects the repairs and resale costs that buyer takes on.

Compare written offers line by line: price, who pays transfer tax and recording, repair credits, and the closing date. Ask the closing attorney to include language on the January 1 owner's tax liability, and confirm that the deed is recorded promptly. A house with liens, tenants or an unsettled estate may need extra steps, so raise those facts with every buyer at the start.

faqs.q: Do I still owe Coweta property tax if I sell my Newnan house this year?
faqs.a: Possibly. Coweta bills the owner of record on January 1 and also mails a bill to the newest owner on the Assessors' records. Put the tax payment duty in the contract and settle it at closing so the bill is paid by the due date.

faqs.q: When is the appeal deadline for a Newnan assessment?
faqs.a: It is 45 days from the date on the assessment notice. For 2026 the Coweta deadline was August 3. Call the Assessors at 770-254-2680 for the date on a future notice.

faqs.q: Does Newnan have historic districts that affect repairs?
faqs.a: Yes. The city lists seven historic districts, including Cole Town, College-Temple, Downtown and the newly listed Chalk Level. Call Planning and Zoning at 770-254-2354 to ask whether exterior work on your address needs review.

faqs.q: What does Georgia charge on a house sale recorded in Coweta County?
faqs.a: The state transfer tax is $1 for the first $1,000 and 10 cents for every additional $100 or fraction. The Coweta clerk also charges $25 to record a deed. The PT-61 form must be e-filed with the title change.

faqs.q: Who files the deed after a Newnan closing?
faqs.a: Usually the closing attorney or title company. Coweta's clerk allows licensed attorneys, lenders and title companies to file on paper, while self-filers must e-file after identity verification.
